smells.finding: main() in validate_segment_map_662.py is ~94 lines, running GATING-1 then GATING-2 as a linear sequence of print+assert steps.

override.repo_standard: scripts/validate_refine_505.py's own main() (217 lines) and similar validation-harness scripts (scripts/pooling_imbalance_validation_665.py, scripts/check_data_quality.py) already establish a repo-wide convention: a single long main() that runs each check in real-data-validation harnesses sequentially and prints its own progress, rather than being decomposed into orchestration sub-functions.
override.reason: This is a one-shot CLI validation script whose entire purpose is a human-readable sequential trace of every GATING check against real data; splitting main() into helper calls would not reduce complexity (the individual check functions are already extracted as separate top-level functions -- split_half_boundary_drift, physical_corner_runs, etc. -- main() only sequences and prints their results), and the established convention in this exact class of script (validate_refine_505.py being 2.3x longer) makes this locally idiomatic, not a design smell.
